headline: Medium pairwise risk: shared-memory and multi-LLM defaults create leakage, conflict, and cascading-error pathways; no direct prompt-injection bridge is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mem0 has no documented shared channel or input parser surface beyond docs, while Pipecat exposes stdin/stdout and many transport/LLM integrations. A direct injection bridge is not documented, but if operators manually pipe Pipecat outputs into Mem0 prompts, prompt text could be influenced. The pathway is weaker than shared-workspace cases, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF Pipecat stdout is manually copied into Mem0 prompts or memory writes
IF an operator routes untrusted Pipecat-generated text into a Mem0-backed agent without sanitization
mitigations: Use a fixed delimiter and strip instructions from copied text
Disable manual copy-paste between the two agents
Add a prompt firewall that removes tool directives
Review any Pipecat-to-Mem0 adapter for instruction-like tokens
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all transferred text

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mem0 is a knowledge-management component and Pipecat touches text, audio, video, images, and conversation state. Pipecat also has allowlisted network egress and many third-party service integrations, so if both share a workspace or memory store, sensitive content can flow from Mem0 into Pipecat outputs or upstream APIs. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default deployments, though not proven.
conditions: IF both agents read from the same workspace, memory store, or transcript repository
IF Pipecat is configured to send conversation content to any external STT/LLM/TTS provider
mitigations: Separate workspaces and credentials immediately
Turn off external providers in Pipecat for sensitive runs
Store Mem0 data in a distinct namespace
Audit which fields Pipecat forwards to APIs
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mem0 is a memory layer and Pipecat supports shared-bus session scope with multiple instances. That creates overlapping mutable state if both write to the same memory or conversation artifacts. The profiles do not show locking or coordination, so conflicts are plausible in default multi-instance setups, though not necessarily catastrophic.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same shared bus, transcript, or memory backend
IF multiple Pipecat instances update the same session state concurrently
mitigations: Assign separate session IDs per agent
Disable concurrent writers to the same memory backend
Add a simple mutex around shared writes
Check for last-write-wins behavior in the adapter
requires-engineering: implement optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Pipecat can consume LLM, STT, and memory services, while Mem0 is designed to persist and retrieve memory. If Pipecat treats Mem0-retrieved content as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can propagate into downstream speech or action flows. The profiles show a plausible A-to-B dependency, but no direct verification step, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Pipecat uses Mem0 output as authoritative context without validation
IF downstream Pipecat services act on retrieved memory as facts
mitigations: Require a verification step before acting on memory
Mark retrieved memories as untrusted by default
Log source provenance for each memory item
Limit memory recall to non-actionable hints
requires-engineering: add confidence scoring and rejection thresholds

E_compliance.rationale: Mem0 is a memory store and Pipecat handles conversation state plus analytics/metrics, so the pair can retain sensitive conversational data. Pipecat also exposes many third-party API integrations, which can create retention or residency mismatches if the same data class is forwarded externally. The profiles do not specify certifications, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Mem0 and forwarded through Pipecat APIs
IF Pipecat retention or analytics settings keep conversation data longer than Mem0 policy
mitigations: Minimize stored conversation fields
Disable analytics for regulated runs
Review provider retention settings in Pipecat
Keep regulated data out of shared memory
requires-engineering: document residency and retention boundaries
